newsitem.title: EGYPT: Oman says will comply with Arab decisions on Israel.
newsitem.headline: Oman says will comply with Arab decisions on Israel.

text.p: Oman said on Monday it would comply with an Arab League resolution recommending Arab states stop normal relations with Israel in response to the Jewish state's settlement policy in Jerusalem.

"Those relations which have been built with the previous (Israeli) government are not going to exist," Omani Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Youssef bin Alawi bin Abdullah told reporters at the Arab League.
"This (resolution) is a consensus in the Arab world to close all normalisation with Israel unless Israel changes its course or present policy. Oman will follow this resolution," he added.
Israel has opened a trade office in the Omani capital Muscat and Oman opened a similar office in Tel Aviv last August -- the first Gulf state to do so.
Earlier this month Oman said it had frozen ties with Israel but the offices remain open.
Asked if and when the Israeli office in Oman would shut down, Alawi said: "Most probably...When it is necessary."
Alawi was speaking on arrival at Arab League headquarters for the closing session of a two-day foreign ministers meeting.
The meeting is expected formally to endorse the resolution, which also suggest withdrawing from multilateral Middle East talks and reactivating the Arab boycott of Israel.
